knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Logarithmic Function With a General Base

question.:question/worked-solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{a}x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}a}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{'}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{11}x-10\operatorname{ln}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{11}x)-10\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}(11)}-10(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}(11)}-\frac{10}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: x>0; logarithm base positive and unequal to1; integer base2..12

question.:question/problem:
Given the function $y=7{x}^{2}-5\log_{4}x,$ find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$ Give an exact answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is
{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{a}x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{2}-5\log_{4}x) \\  & =7\cdot 2x-5\cdot \frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}4} \\  & =14x-\frac{5}{x\operatorname{ln}4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(14x-\frac{5}{x\operatorname{ln}4})|}_{x=1} \\  & =14(1)-\frac{5}{1\cdot \operatorname{ln}4} \\  & =14-\frac{5}{\operatorname{ln}4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6\log_{12}x-12\ln x+12e^{x}) \\ & =\frac{6}{x\ln 12}-\frac{12}{x}+12e^{x} \\ & =12 e^{x} - \frac{12}{x} + \frac{6}{x \ln{\left(12 \right)}}.\end{aligned}
